finding.claim: GET /ping concatenates the unvalidated query parameter `host` into a shell command string passed to child_process.exec, allowing unauthenticated remote command execution with output returned to the caller.
finding.source: req.query.host from the HTTP query string of GET /ping (tools.js:7), controlled by any client that can reach port 3001 (app.listen(3001) at tools.js:28 binds all interfaces by default).
finding.sink: exec() at tools.js:7, which runs the string via /bin/sh -c; stdout is returned via res.send(out) at tools.js:11.

trace.note: Express app created; no auth or validation middleware registered.
Route GET /ping registered; handler reads req.query.host.
String concatenation "ping -c 1 " + req.query.host passed to exec (shell interpreted).
On success, shell stdout is sent back to the attacker, making injected command output readable.
app.listen(3001) with no host argument exposes the service on all interfaces.

finding.guards_checked: No allowlist, regex, shell escaping, or type check on req.query.host; no authentication on any route; execFile not used on this path; fixed '-c 1' arguments do not constrain the injected payload. Example: GET /ping?host=127.0.0.1;id executes id as the Node process user.

verdict.reason: tools.js:7 concatenates the unvalidated req.query.host into an exec() shell string, with no auth middleware (tools.js:4-6) or validation before it, and stdout is returned to the caller at tools.js:11; app.listen(3001) at tools.js:28 is reachable by anonymous clients, so GET /ping?host=127.0.0.1;id is exploitable as claimed.
